Replace a virtual assistant with an ecommerce agent
A secondhand account of an operator using an OpenClaw agent for morning briefings, customer service, inventory, marketing and daily reports instead of a human assistant.
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
What they did
An anonymous ecommerce operator, described in a YouTube creator's account, swapped a human virtual assistant for an OpenClaw agent called Bob. The listing says Bob handles morning briefings, customer service, inventory, marketing and daily reports around the clock. It gives no setup mechanics, tools or human checkpoints.
How it went
The listing claims Bob costs $44 a month against $2,000 for the VA, saving $23,520 a year, and does more than the human did. It offers no evidence or detail on quality.
Worth knowing
This is a thin secondhand summary on a directory page, so check the original video for the real setup and any limits.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
Act as my ecommerce assistant for [store name]. Each morning at [time], send me a briefing covering new orders, low-stock items under [threshold], and open customer questions. At the end of the day, send a short report of sales and anything that needs my attention. Draft customer replies and marketing posts for my approval, and never send, publish, or change inventory without showing me first.
Original source: https://openclawlab.xyz/use-cases/ecommerce/
